Because relatively few vaccinated participants possessed each inferred HLA allele, we intentionally applied permissive enrichment criteria to maximize sensitivity and retain potentially informative sequences (odds ratio > 1; Fisher's exact test p < 0.5).
Clonotypes were retained if they demonstrated both substantial expansion (fold change > 2) and statistical significant change in template counts (FDR-adjusted Fisher's exact test p < 0.05).

findings.sentence: A doubling of urinary cadmium (eg, from the median of 0.29 µg/L to 0.58 µg/L) was associated with 1.71-1.92 fewer years of survival time at the 10th percentile, 1.50-1.67 fewer years at the 25th percentile, and 1.35-1.53 fewer years at the median across the five imputations (n = 7,061; 1,510 deaths; all p ≤ 0.0017; table 2).

A doubling of whole-blood lead (eg, from 1.57 µg/dL to 3.14 µg/dL) was associated with 0.63-0.71 fewer years at the 10th percentile, 0.55-0.65 at the 25th percentile, and 0.61-0.63 at the median (n = 24,021; 6,885 deaths; all p ≤ 0.0051), with the largest reduction at τ = 0.10; the median was not estimable in two imputations (table 2).

Urinary arsenic was not associated with survival time at any quantile (β 0.04 to 0.32 years at τ = 0.10 and 0.33 to 0.54 years at τ = 0.25; all 95% CIs included zero; p ≥ 0.14; n = 5,552; 960 deaths); the median was estimable in two imputations only (table 2).
